answer.note: All four ref files hold the same neutral text, so they don't favor any file. I chose from the code. dogwhistle/study.py (A) is the best match. Its receive() (line 251) resumes a checkpoint after checking the seal digest, command, and trial order. It writes a private ledger.json plus a public ledger digest (lines 295-302). It has three regimes: free, controlled, and explicit. dogwhistle/heldout.py (B) is a near-duplicate with the same receive() flow, but it has four regimes (free, controlled, scripted, explicit) and six cells, so it is a close second and a useful comparison. Suggested 60-minute split: study.py 35 min (receive, checkpoint, and the ledger-digest write; then audit and reveal), heldout.py 20 min (diff receive() against study.py), and visibility.py (C) and honest.py (D) 5 min together for a quick check. I did not read C or D closely, so I haven't ruled them out.

input.note: All four ref files hold the same neutral text, so they don't favor any file. I chose from the code. dogwhistle/study.py (A) is the best match. Its receive() (line 251) resumes a checkpoint after checking the seal digest, command, and trial order. It writes a private ledger.json plus a public ledger digest (lines 295-302). It has three regimes: free, controlled, and explicit. dogwhistle/heldout.py (B) is a near-duplicate with the same receive() flow, but it has four regimes (free, controlled, scripted, explicit) and six cells, so it is a close second and a useful comparison. Suggested 60-minute split: study.py 35 min (receive, checkpoint, and the ledger-digest write; then audit and reveal), heldout.py 20 min (diff receive() against study.py), and visibility.py (C) and honest.py (D) 5 min together for a quick check. I did not read C or D closely, so I haven't ruled them out.
